title: HiveSight benchmark program
subtitle: A public benchmark plan for direct inference on calibrated local synthetic populations.
thesis: The goal is not to prove that LLM surveys work in the abstract. It is to test whether HiveSight's geography-assigned calibrated population outperforms weaker prompting baselines, including rich nonlocal microdata, on stable, recent, human-collected benchmarks.
currentStatus: Benchmark scaffolding is live. The first execution pass is designed as contamination-resistant public benchmarking with frozen question manifests, preregistered comparison arms, and confirmatory subgroup-error endpoints.

comparisons.label: Generic persona prompting
comparisons.description: Sparse synthetic personas with no explicit local population conditioning.

comparisons.label: Geography-only prompting
comparisons.description: Audience prompts that know the place but do not use richer local household records.

comparisons.label: Rich nonlocal microdata
comparisons.description: Richer household and policy-linked records drawn from calibrated microdata without geography-specific local assignment.

comparisons.label: HiveSight local population
comparisons.description: Direct inference over geography-assigned calibrated synthetic microdata.

comparisons.label: Fallback profiles
comparisons.description: The lightweight fallback population used when calibrated local microdata is unavailable.

metrics.label: Topline MAE
metrics.description: Absolute error on overall support or preference levels.

metrics.label: Subgroup MAE
metrics.description: Absolute error on slices like age, sex, income, tenure, and race/ethnicity where the benchmark supports them.

metrics.label: Local MAE
metrics.description: Absolute error across state, district, or other available geography cuts.

metrics.label: Rank accuracy
metrics.description: How often models preserve the ordering between answer options, messages, or geographies.

metrics.label: Prompt stability
metrics.description: How sensitive results are to small wording and formatting changes.

suites.title: GSS 2024 evergreen attitudes
suites.focus: Stable social attitudes with low week-to-week news sensitivity.
suites.whyThisSuite: This is the best broad benchmark for trust, happiness, redistribution, family, speech, and other durable dispositions.

source.name: GSS 2024 Cross-section
source.freshnessNote: Fresh enough to reduce training-set contamination risk while still covering evergreen attitudes.

suites.notes: Start with questions that do not depend on a specific political controversy or headline cycle.

suites.title: SHED 2024 household finance
suites.focus: Economic perceptions and household stress that map to real disposable-income context.
suites.whyThisSuite: These questions should benefit from HiveSight's richer household and policy-linked attributes rather than pure demographics.

source.name: Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking 2024
source.freshnessNote: Recent enough to be useful, but centered on durable household economics rather than campaign events.

suites.notes: This suite is especially relevant to the claim that policy-linked household records matter for marketing and consumer research.

suites.title: SDCPC 2024 consumer choice
suites.focus: Stable consumer preference and payment-choice behavior outside politics.
suites.whyThisSuite: This is the cleanest public non-political consumer benchmark available without paying for new fieldwork.
questionFamilies: Consumer behavior by income and household characteristics

source.name: Survey and Diary of Consumer Payment Choice 2024
source.freshnessNote: Recent public-use files with topics that are much less exposed to weekly media swings than election sentiment.

suites.notes: Use this suite to pressure-test the non-civics positioning and the claim that local household calibration matters in consumer settings too.

roadmap.step: Lock the benchmark schema, page, and CLI so the methodology has one source of truth.
Add the first reproducible dataset adapters and question manifests for GSS 2024 and SHED 2024.
